note: Reviewed CDB90 match 235, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The 1 March 1896 battle is Menelik II’s Ethiopian army against Baratieri’s expeditionary force, including Eritrean ascari. Retain each aggregate locally; do not attach the whole Italian-side count to European infantry alone, and do not split Ethiopian forces among commanders. The Ministry of Culture study discusses an expeditionary force exceeding 20000; it does not independently establish the precise CDB 20251 strength or the Ethiopian 120000 estimate. Both remain explicitly attributed source estimates, not exact headcounts or reconstructed orders of battle. These sources review event and force identity; CDB numerical estimates and uncertainty are retained, not independently certified. The Ministry of Defence memorial history instead describes three Italian columns with 14500 men against more than 100000 Ethiopian fighters. The Culture volume’s expeditionary figure does not establish which personnel were present on 1 March. This review found no affirmative evidence identifying absent formations inside the CDB total, so the disagreement alone is not treated as proof of a scope error. Neither institutional estimate replaces the CDB values. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name ETH ARMY): The sources identify Menelik’s Ethiopian army and Baratieri’s Italian/Eritrean force. CDB estimates remain unchanged. The Defence memorial history gives 14500 men in three Italian columns against over 100000 Ethiopian fighters; the Culture study’s expeditionary figure exceeds 20000. These differing accounts do not independently certify the CDB battle strengths. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name IT ARMY): The sources identify Menelik’s Ethiopian army and Baratieri’s Italian/Eritrean force. CDB estimates remain unchanged. The Defence memorial history gives 14500 men in three Italian columns against over 100000 Ethiopian fighters; the Culture study’s expeditionary figure exceeds 20000. These differing accounts do not independently certify the CDB battle strengths.
